title: App Router 15 — why are params and searchParams now Promises?
description: Next.js 15 makes route params async to support PPR and streaming — you must await them.
answer:
In Next.js 15, `params` and `searchParams` are Promises — you must `await` them in pages, layouts, and `generateMetadata` to unblock Partial Prerendering and streaming.

<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">Next 14</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">params: {id} sync</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">blocking render</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">no PPR hole</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box"/>

<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">searchParams: Promise</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">async opt-in</text>

<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">await params</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">or use(params)</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">codemod: npx</text>

Next.js 15 changes the App Router segment props: `params` and `searchParams` are no longer plain objects but Promises.

A page signature changes from `({ params })` to `({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> })`. This is not just an API annoyance — it lets Next.


| Area | Next 14 | Next 15 |
|---|---|---|
| `params` type | `{ id: string }` | `Promise<{ id: string }>` |
| `searchParams` | object | `Promise<object>` |
| How to read | `params.id` | `const { id } = await params` |

**Interview Tip:** In interviews, explain the why: Promises let Next render the static shell before resolving dynamic params, enabling PPR. Show both server `await` and client `use()` patterns.

```js
// app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx — Next 15
type Props = { params: Promise<{slug:string}>, searchParams: Promise<{q?:string}> };
export default async function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {
  const { slug } = await params;
  const { q } = await searchParams;
  const post = await db.post.findUnique({ where: { slug } });
  if (!post) notFound();
```

title: Server Components and external packages — what does `serverComponentsExternalPackages` do?
description: Control which Node packages stay external to the Server Component bundle and run with native APIs.
answer:
`serverComponentsExternalPackages` tells Next not to bundle heavy/native Node packages into the RSC graph — they run as external Node requires, fixing native addon errors.

<rect x="40" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box"/>
<text x="150" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22c55e">Bundled</text>
<text x="150" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">pure JS libs</text>
<text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">tree-shaken</text>
<text x="150" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">fast cold</text>
<rect x="300" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box"/>
<text x="410" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#f59e0b">External</text>
<text x="410" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">sharp, prisma, pg</text>
<text x="410" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">native binary</text>
<text x="410" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">require at runtime</text>
<rect x="560" y="40" width="220" height="90" rx="14" class="d-box"/>
<text x="670" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#3b82f6">Config</text>
<text x="670" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">serverComponentsExternal</text>
<text x="670" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">array of names</text>
<text x="670" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" class="d-sub">no client bundle</text>
<path d="M 266 85 H 294" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
<path d="M 526 85 H 554" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
</svg>

Server Components run in Node, but Next still bundles their dependency graph to optimize and trace imports.

Packages with native binaries (`sharp`, `prisma`, `bcrypt`, `pg`, `canvas`, `puppeteer`) or that do dynamic `require()` break when bundled — you see errors like `Module not found: Can't resolve 'sharp'` or `prisma is not a function`. Listing them in `next.config.js` under `experimental.


| Package type | Bundle? | Example | Symptom if bundled |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pure JS (zod, date-fns) | yes | `zod` | fine |
| Native binary | external | `sharp` | `Cannot find module sharp` |
| ORM client | external | `prisma` | runtime init fails |
| Mixed (needs both) | external server, bundle client | `react-pdf` | SSR crash |

**Interview Tip:** Name-drop `sharp` and `prisma` as canonical examples. Explain the fix is keeping native requires external so Node loads the binary at runtime.

```js
// next.config.ts — keep native packages external to RSC bundle
const nextConfig = {
  // Next 15 stable key (fallback: experimental.serverComponentsExternalPackages)
  serverExternalPackages: ['sharp', 'prisma', '@prisma/client', 'bcrypt'],
};
export default nextConfig;
// app/api/image/route.ts — can now use sharp safely
import sharp from 'sharp';
export async function GET(){ const buf = await sharp('./photo.jpg').resize(800).toBuffer(); return new Response(buf,{headers:{'Content-Type':'image/jpeg'}}); }
```

title: next/font and next/image — how do they combine for Core Web Vitals?
description: Using both optimizers together to fix LCP, CLS, and bandwidth — automatic `priority`, `sizes`, and font fallbacks.
answer:
Pair `next/image` (`priority`, `sizes`, `placeholder`) for LCP with `next/font` `size-adjust` fallbacks for CLS — both self-host and preload from your domain. Core Web Vitals wins come from pairing the two: `next/image` fixes LCP — it generates `srcset`/`sizes`, serves AVIF/WebP, lazy-loads by default, and when you add `priority` to the above-the-fold hero image it preloads that image with `fetchpriority=high`. title: PPR vs ISR vs SSR — how do you pick the rendering strategy in Next 15?
description: Decision matrix for static, ISR, SSR, and PPR — covering freshness, TTFB, and CDN costs.
answer:
Use PPR for mixed pages (static shell + personalized holes), ISR for time-based revalidation, SSR/dynamic for fully per-request data — PPR gives CDN speed with per-request holes.

In Next 15 the choice is not binary static vs dynamic — PPR sits in the middle.

Use **Static/ISR** (`export const revalidate = 60` or `'use cache'` with `cacheLife`) when freshness tolerance is minutes/hours and the whole page can share one TTL (blog posts, product catalog). TTFB is CDN-fast, cost is low, but data is stale until revalidation.


| Strategy | Config | TTFB | Freshness | Cost | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Static | `force-static` | CDN fast | stale | low | docs |
| ISR | `revalidate: 60` | CDN fast | minutes stale | low | blog |
| PPR | `ppr:'incremental'` + `Suspense` | fast (shell CDN) | per-hole fresh | medium | PDP, feed |

**Interview Tip:** Frame as freshness vs TTFB: ISR whole-page TTL, PPR per-hole freshness, SSR always fresh but slow — recommend PPR for mixed e-commerce pages.
